newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks at six-year high, further gains seen.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks at six-year high, further gains seen.

text.p: Taiwan's stock index sliced through resistance to close at a six-year high on Wednesday as officials' market-boosting comments eased investor jitters over central bank monetary policy.
Brokers said Wednesday's ebullient trade, which lifted the index to its highest level since 1990, had given the market enough momentum to soar as high as 8,400 in the near term.
The index ended 62.89 points or 0.79 percent higher at 8,019.46 after spiking to an intra-day peak of 8,049.94.
Wednesday's close surpassed the 7,983.71 finish on Saturday and marked the index's highest level since it reached 8,059.14 on May 16, 1990.
Turnover was a hectic T$143.606 billion.
Securities and Exchange Commission chairman Lu Tung-ying said on late Tuesday that the market's heavy recent turnover was acceptable as long as trading remained orderly and healthy.
"Positive statements by government officials were the major reason for the gains," said George Hou, fund manager of Jardine Fleming Securities.
"Investors renewed their confidence, which had been dampened by the central bank's call for caution," Hou added.
Transport shares, buoyed by prospects for direct shipping between Taiwan and rival China, surged 3.07 percent with First Steamship, rising T$1.60 to close at T$25.50.
Chemical issues surged 2.08 percent, with China Chemical rising T$2.10 to T$34.80.
Automotive shares were the only losing sector, falling 0.42 percent on profit-taking, brokers said.
Analysts said they expected the market to rise further in the near term now that it has broken through psychological resistance at 8,000 points.
"No resistance is seen for the market until at least the 8,400 level," said Oliver Fang, senior analyst for National Securities.
The index, bolstered by widespread expectations that Taiwan's economic recovery was picking up steam, has gained more than 1,000 points in 1997.

Analysts said the recent frantic trading could get another boost if Taiwan launches domestic futures trading by October, something made possible after months of delay by the passage on Tuesday of a Futures Trading Law in parliament.
A trading range of 7,900 to 8,200 was expected on Thursday.
